content: 1. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, the dose of abemaciclib should be increased to the level prior to initiating the strong inhibitor. Close monitoring is required. 2. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of abrocitinib by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. When coadministered with CYP2C19 inhibitors, start abrocitinib at 50 mg daily. If an adequate response is not achieved after 12 weeks, the dose may be increased to 100 mg daily. 3. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of abrocitinib by decreasing its metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Abrocitinib is a substrate of CYP2C9 and CYP2C19. Moderate-to-strong inhibitors of both enzymes increase systemic exposure to abrocitinib and its active metabolites, potentially increasing adverse effects. 4. Omeprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be used. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases as gastric pH increases. 5. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of acalabrutinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of acalabrutinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt treatment with acalabrutinib. 6. Acetazolamide increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Acetazolamide also increases the level or effect of omeprazole by affecting the same enzyme. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 7. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of adagrasib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, should not be coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until steady-state concentrations are reached (approximately 8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases adagrasib concentrations and the risk of toxicities. 8. Clarithromycin and adagrasib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsade de Pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. If coadministration is unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is recommended. 9. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The cytotoxic component DM1 is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, and strong inhibitors of this enzyme may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. 10. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If afatinib is not tolerated when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of afatinib by 10 mg. 11. Albuterol and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of alfentanil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Alfuzosin and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin also increases the level or effect of alfuzosin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 14. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of aliskiren by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of almotriptan by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of alosetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Omeprazole increases the level of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases the level or effect of alprazolam by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of alvimopan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of ambrisentan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases the level or effect of ambrisentan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 20. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of amiodarone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if coadministered. 23. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of amitriptyline by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of amlodipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, decreased heart rate, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Amobarbital decreases the level or effect of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. It also decreases the level of clarithromycin by increasing its elimination and by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 26. Amoxapine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of amoxicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Omeprazole decreases the level or effect of amphetamine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of ampicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Clarithromycin and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Anastrozole increases the level or effect of omeprazole and clarithromycin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 32. Clarithromycin increases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by decreasing their metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of apalutamide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of omeprazole and clarithromycin by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
